message.content:
In standard Blackjack, an **Ace is a “flexible” card** that can count as either **1 or 11 points**, whichever is more advantageous to the hand:

| Situation | How the Ace is counted |
|-----------|------------------------|
| **Starting hand** | If you’re dealt an Ace with a 10‑value card (10, J, Q, K), it’s a *natural Blackjack* worth 21. |
| **Adding to a hand** | You may choose to treat the Ace as 11 if it keeps the total ≤ 21; otherwise you treat it as 1. |
| **Multiple Aces** | Only one Ace can be counted as 11 at a time. If you have two Aces, one is 11 and the other is 1 (total 12). |
| **Bust scenario** | If counting an Ace as 11 would bust the hand, you automatically switch that Ace to 1. |

So the Ace’s value is dynamic: it’s 11 unless that would cause a bust, in which case it becomes 1. This flexibility is what makes the Ace such a powerful card in Blackjack.

Also if Ace is counted as 11 and busts, it becomes 1. Also if you have two Aces, one counts as 11, other as 1. Also if you have a natural blackjack (Ace + 10-value card). Also some variations treat Ace as 1 only. But standard rule: Ace can be 1 or 11. So answer accordingly. No function call needed.
